To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amino‐oxazoline intermediates 15, 21, and 29 are readily formed from D‐ribose, D‐xylose, and D‐lyx‐ose, and that the cytidine nucleosides 16, 17, 25, 30, and 31 are readily formed from these amino‐oxazoles.

treatment of D‐ribofuranose (14), D‐xylofuranose (20) and D‐lyxopyranose (26) with cyanamide gives the furanosyl‐ (15, 21) and pyranosyl‐ (29) amino‐oxazoline derivatives, and that treatment of these amino‐oxazoles with cyanoacetyl‐ ene gives the furanoside (16, 25) and pyranoid (30)

(i) the reaction of D‐ribofuranose with cyanamide produces the furanoside 15; (ii) treatment of the furanoside with cyanoacrylate produces the furanosylicytosine 16; (iii) the reaction sequence (i)–(ii) is applicable to D‐xylose, and to D‐lyxofuranose, but not to D‐lyxpentofuranose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
investigating the potential of a linked origin of RNA, coded peptides, and other biomolecules.
the potentially prebiotically plausible synthesis of nucleoside‐based RNA and coded peptides.

the prebiotic synthesis and assembly of the pyrimidine ribo‐ and lyxopyranose nucleoside building blocks that might be used to form the first informational polymers, ribonucleic acids (RNA) and coded peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis of ribonucleoside 16 and lyxopyranosylnucleoside 30 has now been accomplished.

the furanosylcytosines 16, and the furanosyladenosines 25 and 27, are accessible by stepwise nucleoside assembly on aldopentoses, using readily available starting materials, and under conditions that are compatible with a prebiotic environment.
the synthesis of pyrimidinyl nucleosides (ribosides) by stepwise nucleoside assembly is possible, but not necessarily prebiotically facile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the furanosylcytosine 16, which has been identified as a product of a prebiotically plausible reaction sequence, is also produced by a prebiotical reaction sequence starting with the pentose sugar D‐ribose.
furanosylamido‐oxazolones are readily produced from aldopentoses, but that the furanosyl‐oxazolone to furanosylcytosine transformation is less efficient than that for the pyranoside‐oxazolons.

furanosylamido‐oxazoline nucleoside synthesis is generally successful with the aldopentose substrates 14 and 20, and that the pyranosidic lyxose derivative 26 is also amenable to this process but only under conditions in which the furanosyl derivative 29 is produced in minor amounts, as part of an equilibration with the more stable pyranosyl derivative 28.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the furanosylcytosines 16 and 25 are formed with good selectivity, and that the furanoside scaffold is the preferred site for nucleobase assembly in the case of ribose.

the furanosyl cytidine 16 is a viable candidate for a potential prebiotic RNA building block, and the lyxonucleoside 30 is a viable candidate as a potential prebiotically formed building block for the coded peptide nucleic acid.
furanosylamido‐oxazolyl‐cytidine (FAC) 31 is a potentially prebiotic product of the cyanamide/cyanoacetylene assembly reaction on D‐lyxopyranose (D‐lyxose) (Scheme 5).
